posts.text:
“Beyond dystopian.”

Novelist Dave Eggers is sounding the alarm about AI, which he argues is harming children’s education: 

“You have a ten-year-old who is unprecedented in the history of the world. There's never been anyone like that person… To think about that one-of-a-kind-in-the-history-of-humanity person shopping their vision out to a machine, how tragic that is. That's beyond dystopian. It cannot be allowed. Not even one ounce of AI can be allowed in the humanities and youth education.”
posts.summary: Amplifies concerns that AI harms children's education and development

posts.text: “It scares me when people aren’t brave enough to face their history.” @smithsonian Secretary Lonnie Bunch has been criticized by the Trump administration, but he tells me his mission is unchanged: “We try to tell a complicated story that is driven by the best nonpartisan scholarship we have.”
posts.summary: Defends Smithsonian's nonpartisan scholarship amid Trump criticism
posts.quote: “It scares me when people aren’t brave enough to face their history.” @smithsonian Secretary Lonnie Bunch has been criticized by the Trump administration, but he tells me his mission is unchanged: “We try to tell a complicated story that is driven by the best nonpartisan scholarship we have.”

posts.text: As America turns 250, “it’s really important that we have a commitment to telling the complete story of America,” @smithsonian head Lonnie Bunch tells me. “Our job is to say, how do we tell an accurate history… that challenges America to live up to its ideals?”
posts.summary: Emphasizes importance of complete, accurate American history and ideals

posts.text: After 1,000 days of war, the mood in Israel is "somber ... but very much angry," political analyst @dahliasc tells me. Ahead of elections later this year, she tells me why some people are calling Netanyahu's coalition, "the government of the massacre".
posts.summary: Reports Israeli public anger and criticism of Netanyahu's wartime governance
posts.quote: After 1,000 days of war, the mood in Israel is "somber ... but very much angry," political analyst @dahliasc tells me. Ahead of elections later this year, she tells me why some people are calling Netanyahu's coalition, "the government of the massacre".

posts.text: Benjamin Netanyahu "needs a war" to stay in power, argues Ami Ayalon, former director of Israeli intelligence service Shin Bet. He tells me why he thinks the Israeli prime minister may be "sacrificing the future of Israel" in his pursuit of eternal war.
posts.summary: Airs argument that Netanyahu pursues eternal war at Israel's expense

posts.text: "They are grinding up men on the battlefield every day." Fmr. NATO Deputy Secretary General Rose Gottemoeller tells me she's not sure how Russia will recover from the huge casualties caused by its invasion of Ukraine.
posts.summary: Highlights massive Russian casualties as indicator of recovery difficulty

posts.text: "Like covering smoke." @jonathanvswan explains why writing his and @maggieNYT's new book, "Regime Change", exploring Trump's second term, almost "killed" them.
posts.summary: Frames Trump's second term as unprecedented and difficult to document
posts.quote: "Like covering smoke." @jonathanvswan explains why writing his and @maggieNYT's new book, "Regime Change", exploring Trump's second term, almost "killed" them.

posts.text: Trump's "net worth is off the charts, bigger than what it was prior to this presidency." @maggieNYT says we're just scratching the surface when it comes to how Trump has used the presidency to inflate his wealth.
posts.summary: Reports Trump used presidency to significantly increase personal wealth
posts.quote: Trump's "net worth is off the charts, bigger than what it was prior to this presidency." @maggieNYT says we're just scratching the surface when it comes to how Trump has used the presidency to inflate his wealth.

posts.text: "We were covering a form of regime change in our own country." @jonathanvswan and @maggieNYT tell me how it quickly dawned on them that Trump's second stint in the White House would be "different from any US Presidency that we've ever seen."
posts.summary: Characterizes Trump's second presidency as uniquely different from all predecessors

posts.text: Ten years since the Brexit vote shook British politics to its core, @annacooban travels to the English town of Hastings, where locals are facing some hard truths about voting to leave the EU in 2016.
posts.summary: Examines Brexit's lasting impact on communities and voter doubts

posts.text: "I've had to fight myself every day to remind myself that I had a father. He existed. He lived with me. I knew him... It's not just in my head." Syrian activist @WafaMustafa9 tells me about her search for the truth about her father, imprisoned under Assad. "I hope my dad knows... that I will not give up on him."
